source_read: https://www.hungryhorse.co.uk/api/menus/getmenudetails/<pub>/<menu> (the JSON each pub's own menu page loads; all 86 files of the 41-pub set re-downloaded 2026-10-08; robots.txt allows /api/menus/), plus the rendered page https://www.hungryhorse.co.uk/pubs/bedfordshire/chequers/menu and the Capelrig (Scottish) page
notes: Calories-only chain, allergens link-only (the per-dish matrix is on Smart Chef, robots Disallow: /). Re-running hungry_horse.py on the fresh files changed no calorie, only the 'seen on N of 41 pubs' note counts of 7 sides, so data/source was refreshed (checked_on 2026-10-08). My own parse of the 86 JSON files matches every one of the 221 items on name and calories (18 manually-named variants checked against the product descriptions: dips, custard vs vegan ice cream, Lorne vs pork sausage, soup bread, Scottish breakfasts), all 37 kids' sugar/salt figures, and the vegetarian tags (dietaryOptions). 8 of the 12 audit-sample rows were also read on the rendered pub pages (933, 502, 1385, 1213, 523, 925, 450, 507 with 5.6 g sugar/2.88 g salt); the other 4 (Salt & Pepper Chips 416, Scampi & Chips 922, Lentil Soup 378, Duo of Meats 892) are on other pubs' pages and were checked in the JSON only. Script fix: fetch() read robots.txt with Python's default agent (403, treated as disallow-all by urllib.robotparser) so a fresh --fetch refused to run; it now uses the browser User-Agent and robots_rfc. Still held back: Pork Sausages (no gluten containing ingredients), whose own text prints salt as '1.92kg'.
